The Rise of the Gig Economy
Many high school graduates are bypassing traditional part-time jobs in retail or fast food to
explore freelancing platforms online. From graphic design to video editing, young people are
turning their hobbies into lucrative side hustles. While this provides unparalleled flexibility
and allows them to build an early professional portfolio, it demands a high level of self-
discipline. Without fixed working hours, procrastination can quickly jeopardize deadlines and
damage client relationships.
1. From the passage, we know that freelancing...
A is less demanding than traditional retail employment.
B requires strong time-management skills to be successful.
C guarantees financial stability for young high school graduates.
To: rajan@mail.com
Subject: Digital Detox Challenge
Dear Rajan,
I noticed you’ve been feeling incredibly burned out lately due to our heavy exam preparation
schedule. Have you considered taking part in the school’s upcoming 'Digital Detox' weekend?
I know we rely heavily on our group chats for study updates, but completely stepping away
from screens for 48 hours might clear your mind. Instead of scrolling through social media
during your study breaks, we could go for a run at the park. Let me know if you want to sign
up together!
From,
Amir
2. According to the email, Amir is...
A advising Rajan to change his study schedule entirely.
B suggesting an offline activity to help Rajan cope with stress.
C complaining about the lack of communication in their study group.
Sarah: Hi Joshua, did you attend the career seminar on Artificial Intelligence yesterday?

Joshua: Yes, I did. It was fascinating, though a bit alarming. The speaker emphasized that
many routine jobs will be fully automated within the next decade.
Sarah: That sounds intimidating. Does it mean we shouldn't pursue traditional degrees like
accountancy or law?
Joshua: Not necessarily, but it means we need to focus heavily on developing analytical and
soft skills that AI cannot easily replicate.
3. From the conversation, we can conclude that...
A traditional career will completely disappear in ten years.
B AI technology will replace the need for higher education.
C human-centric soft skills are vital for future job security.
Master Your Money: Financial Literacy Workshop for Teens!
Are you unsure of how to budget your monthly allowance? Do you find yourself broke by the
third week of the month? Join our interactive workshop this Saturday at 2:00 p.m. at the
Community Library. Learn the difference between "wants" and "needs," discover the power
of compound interest, and get hands-on experience using budgeting apps. Seating is limited
to the first 30 participants. Standard registration closes on Friday.
4. Based on the advertisement, the workshop...
A requires participants to register before Saturday.
B guarantees financial wealth to all attendees.
C is held online due to limited seating capacity.
Fast Fashion vs. Sustainable Thrift
The appeal of fast fashion lies in its ability to rapidly replicate high-end runway designs at low
costs. However, this hyper-production cycle inflicts massive environmental toll through water
pollution and textile waste. In response, a growing number of eco-conscious teenagers are
turning to upcycling—repurposing old textiles into unique garments. This movement does
more than just divert fabric from landfills; it fosters individual creativity over mass
consumerism.
5. From the text, upcycling is becoming popular because it allows teenagers to...
A copy high-end designer garment accurately.
B buy affordable clothes directly from mass producers.
C express their creativity while protecting the environment.
Cyberbullying Awareness Campaign
Think Before You Type!

Our school's counselling department is launching the annual Cyberbullying Awareness Week
from October 12th to 16th. Anonymous posting features on modern apps have unfortunately
led to an increase in online harassment. Remember, words spoken behind a screen carry real-
world consequences. We invite all upper-secondary students to submit original digital posters
or short videos highlighting online kindness. Submit your entries to Room 4B by October 10th
for a chance to win bookstore vouchers.
6. Which of the following is true about the notice?
A The competition is open to students of all age groups.
B Digital submissions must be handed in prior to the official campaign week.
C The main goal of the campaign is to ban anonymous smartphone applications.
The Psychology of Peer Pressure
Psychologists note that during adolescence, the desire for peer acceptance often overrides
personal logic. This is rooted in brain development, where the reward centers are highly
sensitive to social inclusion. Consequently, teenagers might engage in risky behaviours or
change their aesthetic preferences simply to mirror their friend groups. Recognizing this
subconscious drive is the first step toward cultivating true independence and self-worth.
7. From the text, what motivates teenagers to copy their peers?
A A biological urge to feel socially accepted.
B A lack of personal logic and intelligence.
C Conscious efforts to engage in dangerous activities.
Clean Water Initiative
MELAKA, May 14 – A team of Form 5 students from SMK Malim has won the National
Innovation Award for creating a low-cost, solar-powered water filtration device. Designed
specifically for flood-prone rural areas, the prototype utilizes locally sourced gravel, charcoal,
and UV light to purify murky water. During the exhibition, project leader Melissa stated, "Our
ultimate goal wasn't to win the prize money, but to create something functional that disaster
relief teams can deploy instantly."
8. From the news report, we know that the award-winning device...
A was manufactured using expensive imported resources.
B was designed to assist communities during natural disasters.
C earned the student team a massive corporate business contract.

Navigating Digital Information in the Modern Age
In the modern era, the internet has revolutionized the way we acquire knowledge. With a
single click, teenagers can access vast amounts of information on any topic imaginable.
However, this ease of access presents major (0) obstacles that can hinder genuine learning.
One significant issue is the rampant spread of misinformation online.
Many users rely on social media platforms as their primary news sources, where articles are
frequently (9) __________ without thorough fact-checking. While sensational headlines are
eye-catching, they often (10) __________ the public by exaggerating truths or fabricating
events entirely. Instead, developing critical media literacy skills can help students (11)
__________ credible sources from biased opinions, ensuring they absorb accurate
information.
Another challenge is the decrease in attention spans due to micro-content. Many teenagers
spend hours consuming short-form videos, leading to (12) __________ cognitive habits such
as an inability to focus on long-form reading material. Deep reading is (13) __________ for
building analytical thinking and expanding vocabulary. Therefore, educators recommend
dedicating at least 30 minutes of (14) __________ reading time each day to train the brain to
focus effectively.
Emotional well-being is also deeply impacted by digital habits. The constant comparison with
idealized lifestyles on platforms can induce severe (15) __________ and low self-esteem
among youth. Engaging in offline activities such as journaling, playing team sports, or learning
a physical instrument can (16) __________ psychological distress and build resilience.
By making conscious changes to their media consumption, young individuals can (17)
__________ their academic performance and protect their mental health. Cultivating mindful

master them.

The Public Speaking Competition
The auditorium was drafty and hummed with the low, nervous chatter of waiting participants.
Ethan sat in the third row, staring down at his cue cards until the words blurred into
meaningless black ink. His palms were slick with sweat, and his heart hammered violently
against his ribs. Outside, a gentle morning rain tapped against the glass windows, completely
detached from the emotional storm brewing inside him. He had practiced his speech on
environmental conservation a hundred times in front of his bedroom mirror, but standing in
front of a live panel of judges felt like an entirely different reality.
When the compere called out his name, Ethan felt a sudden, icy wave of panic wash over him.
His legs felt heavy, almost detached from his body, as he walked up the wooden steps to the
stage. He adjusted the microphone, the loud screech of audio feedback causing the audience
to wince. He looked up and met the gaze of the head judge—a stern woman with spectacles
resting on the bridge of her nose, her pen poised over a blank scoring sheet. The silence in
the hall stretched out, heavy and suffocating.
Ethan opened his mouth, but no sound came out. His mind had gone completely blank. He
looked down at his cue cards, but his hands were shaking so severely that he could not find
his place. Panic tightened its grip on his throat. He could feel the collective awkwardness of
the audience, the seconds ticking away like an eternity. He thought of his English teacher,
Mrs. Lim, who had spent countless afternoons after school helping him refine his expressions,
and his classmates who had cheered him on. He did not want to let them down.
Taking a deep, steadying breath, Ethan closed his eyes for a brief second. He pocketed his cue
cards entirely. If he could not read them, he would have to speak from the heart. Opening his
eyes, he looked past the judges toward the back of the auditorium. He began to speak. His
voice was shaky at first, but as he transitioned into the core argument of his speech regarding
the destruction of local rainforests, his tone gained strength and clarity.

He spoke with raw passion, abandoning his rigidly memorized script for natural, evocative
language. The judges sat forward, their expressions shifting from passive politeness to
genuine engagement. Ethan felt a sudden surge of adrenaline; he was no longer just
performing a task, he was delivering a message he truly cared about. When he concluded his
final sentence with an impassioned plea for collective action, the auditorium remained silent
for a heartbeat before erupting into thunderous applause.
As Ethan stepped down from the stage, his legs were still trembling, but the crushing weight
in his chest had completely vanished. He did not care whether he walked away with the first-
place trophy anymore. He had faced his greatest fear on that stage and discovered a resilience
within himself that he never knew existed.
19. What was Ethan doing right before his name was called?
A Discussing his speech topic with other participants.
B Looking anxiously out the window at the rain.
C Reading his speech notes until they became unclear.
D Practicing his delivery in front of a mirror.
20. Ethan felt intimidated on stage because...
A the audio equipment was malfunctioning completely.
B the main judge appeared very strict and unsmiling.
C the auditorium was far too crowded for him to handle.
D he had chosen a topic that the judges disliked.
21. Why did Ethan struggle to begin his speech?
A He was distracted by his classmates in the audience.
B He had forgotten to bring his cue cards up with him.
C He was paralyzed by fear and lost his train of thought.
D He was waiting for the judges to give him permission.
22. What motivated Ethan to overcome his sudden panic?
A The desire to win the first-place prize money.
B The thought of the effort his teacher and friends put into supporting him.
C A supportive nod from the head judge in the front row.
D Realizing that the audience was not paying attention to him.
23. The phrase "seconds ticking away like an eternity" highlights that...
A the competition lasted for many hours.
B Ethan felt that the period of silence lasted a very long time.

C the judges were strictly timing his speech length.
D the auditorium clock was making a loud noise.
24. How did Ethan alter his approach to delivering his speech?
A He decided to read word-for-word from his notes.
B He spoke directly to his English teacher for comfort.
C He put away his notes and spoke spontaneously with genuine emotion.
D He shortened his content significantly to save time.
25. What did Ethan realize by the end of the event?
A Winning trophy is the most effective way to gain confidence.
B Public speaking requires a script to be perfectly memorized.
C Facing his fears helped him realize his personal strength.
D Environmental conservation is not a popular topic among judges.
26. What is the most appropriate title for this story?
A An Expected Triumph
B Finding My Voice
C The Strict Judges
D Environmental Awareness

The Importance of Learning Soft Skills
In today's competitive academic environment, upper-secondary students focus heavily on
scoring straight A's. High test scores are undeniably valuable for university applications and
securing scholarships. However, academic excellence alone is no longer a guarantee of future
workplace success. (27) __________
Soft skills refer to interpersonal traits such as communication, teamwork, adaptability, and
problem-solving. Unlike technical skills, which teach you how to use specific software or
machinery, soft skills dictate how you interact with others. (28) __________ Many employers
note that while they can easily train a new recruit on technical tasks, teaching an employee
emotional intelligence is significantly more difficult.
One crucial soft skill that teenagers should develop early is collaboration. Throughout high
school, students are frequently assigned group projects. (29) __________ Instead, it is an
opportunity to learn how to negotiate, manage differing opinions, and delegate tasks fairly.
Adaptability is another essential trait in the modern fast-paced world. Technology is changing
industries at an unprecedented rate, rendering some jobs obsolete overnight. (30)
__________ Individuals who possess high adaptability view unexpected adjustments as
learning opportunities rather than stressful setbacks.
Furthermore, effective communication is vital for building networks. (31) __________ Being
able to articulate your ideas clearly during a presentation or a simple conversation can set
you apart from others. It also involves active listening, which ensures mutual understanding
and prevents workplace conflicts.
In conclusion, while working hard for excellent academic grades is necessary, balancing that
effort with the development of personal traits is equally crucial. (32) __________ By
cultivating these skills during high school, students prepare themselves to become well-
rounded individuals ready for future challenges.

A These group assignments should not be viewed merely as a chore to get a grade.
B This requires students to memorize complex facts before their final examinations.
C Employers are increasingly prioritizing "soft skills" over raw academic results.
D Therefore, people who cannot cope with change will find it easy to excel.
E It allows you to build trust and professional relationships with colleagues and clients.
F They form the foundation of how well an individual can collaborate within a
professional team.
G These attributes cannot be evaluated through standard written tests but are felt in
daily life.
H This means that workers must constantly learn new systems and adjust to evolving
environments.

EXPLORING FUTURE-PROOF CAREERS
A. Data Science and Analytics
Data analytics involves interpreting complex digital footprints to help businesses make
informed decisions. Professionals in this sector possess strong mathematical and logical skills.
Experts suggest that as industries become highly digitized, the reliance on data analysts will
skyrocket. For students who enjoy solving intricate puzzles and working with statistics, this
field offers immense long-term career stability and competitive salaries.
B. Renewable Energy Engineering
Renewable energy engineering focuses on developing clean alternatives to fossil fuels, such
as solar, wind, and geothermal power systems. This career path plays a fundamental role in
combating global climate change. It is highly suited for students with a passion for physics and
environmental conservation. As countries transition to green economies, professionals in this
field will see high job security and a chance to make a tangible global impact.
C. UI/UX Design (User Interface / User Experience)
UI/UX designers focus on perfecting the visual layout and user friendliness of digital platforms
like applications and websites. This career fuses psychological understanding with digital art.
Designers must analyse human behaviours to create smooth, intuitive navigation
experiences. It is an ideal path for creative individuals who wish to work in tech without
necessarily learning complex software engineering languages.
D. Digital Content Creation
Digital content creation offers an independent, dynamic career path for expressive
individuals. From producing educational videos to hosting podcasts or managing corporate
brand identities online, creators utilize storytelling to capture audiences. This path offers
immense working flexibility and direct creative control. However, it requires a high degree of
entrepreneurial consistency and self-motivation to build a stable income.
E. Healthcare and Biotechnology
Healthcare and biotechnology involve using scientific research to develop advanced medical
treatments and life-saving equipment. This path requires extensive academic study in biology
and chemistry. Spending time in research laboratories allows professionals to solve global
health crises and improve human longevity. This sector remains completely recession-proof,
as the human need for medical advancements is perpetual.

F. Cybersecurity Specialization
Cybersecurity specialists protect confidential organizational data systems from malicious
online attacks and corporate espionage. This profession is excellent for individuals with a
meticulous eye for detail and strong problem-solving capabilities. It carries low risk of
unemployment because digital security is paramount for banking, governance, and
commerce. Specialists continuously update their methods to counter evolving online threats.
